newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING - FURTHER DELAY IN MEN'S DOWNHILL.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING - FURTHER DELAY IN MEN'S DOWNHILL.

text.p: Race organisers on Friday delayed the start of a men's World Cup Alpine skiing downhill by one hour because of bad weather.
Organisers said the race, which had been due to start at 1300 local (1200 GMT), had been moved to 1400 (1300) when it would either go ahead or be called off.
"They must start by two p.m. or they will have to call it off," said one local official. "Frankly, I doubt we'll have a race."
Heavy cloud shrouded the Saslong piste as snow, which began falling in Val Gardena overnight, continued steadily.
Organisers first delayed the race start by half an hour and then decided to delay for a further half hour.
Friday's race had already been rescheduled once, after the Canadian resort of Whistler Mountain was unable to stage it earlier this month due to heavy snow.
Race sources in Val Gardena said that if the downhill was unable to go ahead on Friday it could be staged on Saturday along with another already scheduled for the resort.
Earlier on Friday, World Cup organisers called off a women's downhill in Crans Montana, Switzerland, because of rain and heavy fog.
